newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE AUXERRE, HITZFELD WARNS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE AUXERRE, HITZFELD WARNS.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld has warned the club's fans and players against underestimating Auxerre, the German champions' opponents in Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final.

Hitzfeld expressed surprise on Tuesday that the first-leg match was not yet a sell-out. Dortmund can normally pack their Westfalenstadion ground to capacity for the visit of even the most unglamorous Bundesliga sides.
"The difficulty of our task is being totally understimated in Dortmund," Hitzfeld said. "I can't understand the fans who are leaving us in the lurch now."
The coach rates the French champions highly, despite the fact they are having a poor season. Auxerre lie seventh in the league and were knocked out of the French Cup on Friday.
"Now they'll try to rehabilitate themselves in the Champions' Cup," Hitzfeld warned.

The wily coach, who has transformed Dortmund from Bundesliga also-rans to a member of Europe's soccer elite since taking the helm in 1991, suffered a major blow to his preparations when Matthias Sammer was ruled out with a calf injury.
The libero, Europe's player of the year, sustained heavy brusing in Germany's friendly with Isreal in Tel Aviv last week.
He missed Dortmund's 4-1 Bundesliga win over 1860 Munich on Saturday and has now been advised to rest for 10 days.

Auxerre must do without striker Steve Marlet and defender Franck Rabarivony, who are both sidelined with injuries. But coach Guy Roux's main concern is the form of midfielders Moussa Saib and Sabri Lamouchi.
"We've got a real playing problem," Roux said. "We need the playmakers to return to form."
Hitzfeld is also deprived of captain Michael Zorc because of suspension and Julio Cesar and Steffen Freund because of injury. But he believes he has the strength in depth to cope.
"Injuries and suspensions are no excuse any more. We've got 25 players in the squad and all of them are good enough to play in the Champions' Cup," he said.
Wolfgang Feiersinger looks likely to deputise for Sammer, as he did against 1860, although the Austrian international is himself just back from an injury lay-off.
Dortmund fans have fond memories of the last time the two sides met, in the semifinals of the 1993 UEFA Cup. The Germans went through with a dramatic penalty shoot-out victory.
Dortmund lost the final to Juventus but are hoping this could be their year to go one better and lift their first European trophy since winning the Cup Winners' Cup in 1966.
Hitzfeld's side may not just have their own fans behind them in their bid to emulate that triumph over Liverpool in Glasgow's Hampden Park.
Soccer statisticians who love quirky coincidences will be well aware that Dortmund, if they make it to the 1997 final, would be contesting their 100th game in European competition.
Probable teams:
Dortmund - Stefan Klos; Wolfgang Feiersinger, Juergen Kohler, Joerg Heinrich; Stefan Reuter, Paul Lambert, Andreas Moeller, Paulo Sousa, Knut Reinhardt; Karlheinz Riedle, Stephane Chapuisat.
Auxerre - Lionel Charbonnier; Alain Goma, Franck Silvestre, Frederic Danjou, Taribo West; Christina Henna, Philippe Violeau, Sarbri Lamouchi, Moussa Saib; Lilian Laslandes, Bernard Diomede.
